rv.q: All in, it's mad as a shook-up box of frogs, crammed with hilarious lyrics and off-kilter humour.
Inventive, mischievous and thrilling — this is children's theatre that could take on Pixar.
This gloriously weird and subversive musical will please adults and kids alike.
It's not a total smash. Twenty minutes could be lopped off, the dance numbers are a bit loose and some singing has a strong whiff of 'have a go'.
Amy Hodge's production – well-meaning, colourful and jolly as it is – is also half-baked.
This makes for a satisfying and worthwhile addition to the National's laudable track record of making quality entertainment for all the family. Bonkers, but in the best possible way.'
There's no doubt this show is a lot of fun.

Andy Stanton's laugh out loud children's books about a disgusting villain called Mr Gum and the surreal town of Lamonic Bibber have always been more about the wacky world and wordsmithery than the plot.
